Compliance · US

NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 Security and Privacy Controls

NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 · current; minor release 5.2.0 issued 2025-08-27 · mandatory-for-scope · official text (free)

Applies to: US federal information systems (mandatory through FISMA/FIPS 200) and contractors, FedRAMP cloud services, and organisations that adopt the catalogue voluntarily.

  • 1872 points
  • 0 we fix
  • 28 we detect
  • 1844 coming soon
We fix
sloptopop finds evidence of a breach of this point in your code, and at least one of those checks has an automatic fix that has passed review on real code.
We detect
sloptopop finds evidence of a breach of this point in your code, and you fix it.
Coming soon
sloptopop does not check this point yet.

A check shows a breach in code; it does not certify that a point is met. List scraped from the publisher's document on 2026-11-01. A point here means: Family, control, enhancement, lettered and numbered statement part. Withdrawn controls stay, with the source's status. Guidance and assessment procedures left out..

AC Access Control
AC-1 Policy and Procedures
AC-1a Produce and distribute access control policy and procedures to defined recipients.
AC-1a.1 An access control policy must exist at the organization-defined level.
AC-1a.1(a) Policy must cover its aim, reach, responsibilities, leadership backing, coordination and compliance. Coming soon
AC-1a.1(b) Policy must align with relevant laws, orders, regulations and standards. Coming soon
AC-1a.2 Write procedures that help carry out the policy and its controls. Coming soon
AC-1b Appoint an official to oversee creating and distributing the policy and procedures. Coming soon
AC-1c Periodically revisit and revise the policy and procedures.
AC-1c.1 Revise the policy at set intervals and after defined triggering events. Coming soon
AC-1c.2 Revise the procedures at set intervals and after defined triggering events. Coming soon

IA-5 Authenticator ManagementIntroductory statement: authenticators must be managed through the listed activities.

IA-5e Default authenticators must be replaced before first use. We detect

secrets.insecure-defaultA sample signing secret in the env template or CI config is a well-known default authenticator; nothing makes a deployment change it before first use.
IA-5f Change or refresh authenticators on a defined schedule or upon defined events. Coming soon
IA-5g Protect authenticator content from unauthorized disclosure and modification. We detect

secrets.committedEveryone with read access to the repository, its clones and forks can read the credential, so its content is disclosed.

secrets.in-historyAnyone who clones the repository can recover the credential from history, so its content is not protected from disclosure.
IA-5h People must follow, and devices must implement, specific controls protecting authenticators. Coming soon
IA-5i Change group or role account authenticators whenever membership changes. Coming soon

IA-5(1)(a) Keep and refresh a list of common or compromised passwords. Coming soon
IA-5(1)(b) Reject new or changed passwords found on the common or compromised list. Coming soon
IA-5(1)(c) Send passwords only over cryptographically protected channels. Coming soon

IA-5(2) Public Key-based Authentication
IA-5(2)(a) Introductory statement for public key-based authentication requirements.
IA-5(2)(a)(1) Control authorized access to the matching private key. Coming soon
IA-5(2)(a)(2) Map the authenticated key identity to an individual or group account. Coming soon
IA-5(2)(b) Introductory statement for requirements when PKI is used.
IA-5(2)(b)(1) Validate certificates via a certification path to a trust anchor, checking status. We detect

tls.verification-disabledTurning verification off skips certification path validation of the peer's certificate.
IA-5(2)(b)(2) Keep a local cache of revocation data for path validation. Coming soon
IA-5(3) In-person or Trusted External Party RegistrationWithdrawn; folded into the in-person identity proofing enhancement of IA-12. Coming soon

IA-5(5) Change Authenticators Prior to DeliveryDevelopers and installers must supply unique or changed authenticators before delivery. We detect

secrets.insecure-defaultThe developer ships the system with a shared sample signing secret instead of a unique one or a forced change before installation.
IA-5(6) Protection of AuthenticatorsProtect authenticators in proportion to the sensitivity of what they unlock. We detect

secrets.committedCredentials readable by anyone with repository access are concrete evidence those authenticators lack protection suited to what they unlock.
IA-5(7) No Embedded Unencrypted Static AuthenticatorsDo not embed unencrypted static authenticators in applications or static storage. We detect

arch.privileged-key-client-sideThe privileged key is inlined into the client bundle, an unencrypted static authenticator embedded in the application.

secrets.committedA credential committed in plain text is an unencrypted static authenticator embedded in the application's static storage.

secrets.in-historyThe credential stays embedded in the repository's static storage (its history) even after it was removed from the working tree.
IA-5(8) Multiple System AccountsReduce compromise risk from individuals holding accounts on multiple systems. Coming soon

Reuse: US government publication on an official .gov site; reuse terms on the publisher's site (not re-checked); cite IDs and paraphrase. Only identifiers, links and headings are shown, never the text; every summary and note is our own.

The sloptopop CLI and every language library are open source under MIT OR Apache-2.0, at github.com/sloptopop.

Transformations, A to Z: every step from the repository you start with to the branch you get back.

Slop to pop: design patterns: anti-patterns sloptopop converts into design patterns today, with the run that proves each one.

Results: what sloptopop did to every repository it was tested on.

Compliance, point by point and what each check evidences: what sloptopop checks and which controls each check evidences.

This site runs no JavaScript except htmx on the pricing page, to send the waitlist form; every animation is CSS. No cookies, no analytics, no third-party scripts.
